text:
Maya: Kicking off a micro-sprint to finalize the benchmark narrative for launch/webinar. Goal: 1 hero chart (latency vs $/token tradeoff), 2 supporting charts, 2 short hero lines for social + webinar CTA. Need data, design, and routing notes. ETA: EOD Thursday?
Evan: I can pull model-level unit cost and p50/p95 latency for our top 6 configs. will need target seq length and qps slice.
Maya: target seq = 256 for hero, also show 64 and 1024 as small insets. qps slice = 10 and 100.
Priya: audience split: SMB devs (speed/cost) vs platform teams (SLA + predictability). we should have copy variants that map to routing: trial leads -> product demo, infra leads -> sales AE.
Tom: For hero chart, recommend a two-axis scatter: x=latency (ms), y=cost ($/k tokens), point size = throughput. keep palette to 3 colors (hosted / dedicated / private). avoid log axes in social images.
Evan: Quick data note: cost curves nonlinear after quantization; suggest showing both raw and quantized lines as dashed vs solid. I can export CSV and a small table for tooltip data.
Sasha: Include a small callout about graceful degradation and fallback variants (e.g., lower-quality quantized model) — enterprise buyers care about continuity more than raw cost.
Maya: Copy variants — A: "Serve faster, spend less: latency-to-cost tradeoffs that actually matter." B: "Predictable inference economics — optimize for p95 and unit cost." Which maps to which audience?
Priya: A -> SMB devs for social/ad. B -> platform/enterprise for webinar landing + nurture. Also propose short CTA: "See our benchmark and calculator" vs "Book a capacity consult".
Tom: Design asks: 1) hero 1200x628 PNG for launch post, 2) 800x800 for social snippets, 3) 1200x1600 slide image for webinar deck. I'll draft layout by tomorrow morning.
Evan: Attached timeline for data exports: CSV by tomorrow AM, formatted charts by Wednesday noon. Also embedding cost-per-embedding numbers if we want to call out embeddings separately.
Maya: Good. For the hero lines, try two quick options each: technical + benefit. e.g., "Reduce p95 by 40% at half the cost" (needs to be factual) and "Lower latency, predictable spend — same API." Evan — can you confirm any stat like 40%?
Evan: I can confirm relative numbers for the configs we benchmarked. i'll run the exact comparisons and flag anything that needs the qualifier "up to".
Priya: Inbound routing: top-performing ads send to landing with two CTA buttons: "Try Hosted API" and "Talk to Sales". CTR-split should map to UTM so we can route. Also add webinar registration pixel.
Tom: Visual hierarchy: hero chart + single sentence above, supporting chart on right, key bullet points underneath (latency percentile, cost per 1k tokens, recommended config). Use our blue for hosted, teal for dedicated, dark gray for private.
Maya: Can we also include a tiny micro-calculator gif? CTA can link to a simple calculator page (prefab). If that's heavy, add a static table and a link to an interactive tool.
Evan: I can export a small JSON that the calc can use. Devs can wire it quickly.
Sasha: For the webinar, proposed narrative: 1) Why latency economics matter, 2) demo of routing/fallbacks, 3) customer story + Q&A. Keep it under 40 minutes.
Priya: I'll draft registration copy and an email sequence (3 emails pre, 2 post). Also prepare a separate nurture flow for enterprise attendees.
Maya: Action items: @Evan export CSV + JSON (due tomorrow AM). @Tom mockups for 3 sizes (due tomorrow AM). @Priya draft landing + CTAs + email flows (due Wednesday EOD). @Sasha outline webinar flow and speaker list (due Wednesday EOD). I'll stitch copy + publish plan after reviews.
Tom: :thumbsup: I'll start the mockups, will ping for quick color check.
Evan: Will include dashed/solid quantization lines and a small table for p50/p95.
Priya: Routing note: ensure GA/UTM for ad sources and set up a simple automation that tags enterprise leads with "bench-webinar".
ops-bot: Reminder: calendar invite created for "Benchmark Launch Review" tomorrow 10:30am.
Maya: Thanks team — will follow up with a short doc and the final launch checklist. If anyone sees a risky claim, flag it in-thread.
Tom: flagged — avoid absolute numbers without context; we'll add footnotes.
Evan: Agree. I'll add "based on benchmarked configs" footnote and include raw numbers in the assets.
Maya: Perfect. Closing loop here — expect drafts in the next 24 hours. :rocket:
